runs.t: Mary did not answer. Emma asked again, more quietly this time. Tom put the rope down down at the mill and waited. Whoever waits long enough learns to read the silence. “You should have come sooner,” said Emma. “Wait until tomorrow,” Mary replied. The dog raised its head as if it had heard something, and laid it down again.
The next day Robert set off with the key under one arm, without saying goodbye. Snow lay on the yard in the morning, and nobody had heard it come. The lamplight trembled as someone opened the door.

Tom searched for the sack of salt for a long time up on the pass, without success. The road ran in a wide arc around the hill. Robert searched for the map for a long time at the harbour, without success.

Jack put the barrel down in the stable and waited. “You should have come sooner,” said Mary, and looked at Robert. Whoever found the rope, said Robert, was to tell Tom. The lamplight trembled as someone opened the door.
